⠀
Andrew Kolvet built deep ties to American Christian Zionism, major pro-Israel donors, and Israel’s diplomatic and PR apparatus in the United States.
⠀
THE KAIROS COMPANY
⠀
• Kolvet spent four years at The Kairos Company, the PR firm founded by Johnny Moore (former VP of Liberty University)
⠀
• Moore is a key intermediary between U.S. evangelical leaders and the Israeli government
⠀
• At Kairos, Kolvet ran campaigns that overlapped with pro-Israel advocacy
⠀
• The firm also represented PragerU and The Blaze
⠀
FRIENDS OF ZION AND THE ADELSONS
⠀
• In October 2017, Kolvet was listed as media contact for the Jerusalem Prayer Team
⠀
• The campaign, created by the Friends of Zion Heritage Center, claimed 20 million followers
⠀
• Tax filings (Form 990) showed the legal entity was registered as “Friends of the Aden Drug Clinic Inc.,” a Las Vegas methadone clinic
⠀
• Its directors were Sheldon and Miriam Adelson, among the most influential pro-Israel donors in the U.S.
⠀
TURNING POINT USA
⠀
• As TPUSA spokesman and executive producer of The Charlie Kirk Show, Kolvet oversaw the group’s pro-Israel programming
⠀
• TPUSA hosted pro-Israel speakers and fought BDS on campuses
⠀
• In January 2019, he handled PR for the first TPUSA Faith Pastors Tour of Israel, organized with Pastor Rob McCoy
⠀
• He also ran student focus groups. At a Tampa conference, 73% identified as pro-Israel
⠀
TRUMP, ADELSON, NETANYAHU
⠀
• According to Candace Owens, Kirk and Kolvet were present when Trump said, around July 2024, that Miriam Adelson offered $100 million for his campaign in exchange for accepting annexation of the West Bank
⠀
• Kolvet also confirmed that Netanyahu personally called Kirk with an offer of major funding to take TPUSA “to the next level”
⠀
• Kirk turned it down in the Hamptons
⠀
LEAKED CHATS AND THE FBI
⠀
• The MAGA split over Israel surfaced just before Kirk’s assassination in September 2025
⠀
• In October 2025, Owens leaked WhatsApp messages in which Kirk raged over losing a $2 million yearly donation from Robert Shillman
⠀
• Kirk said Jewish donors were “playing into all the stereotypes” and left him “no choice but to leave the pro-Israel cause”
⠀
• Kolvet confirmed the texts on air. He said he was “glad the truth is out,” because Kirk had struggled for months over speech limits on Israel’s policies
⠀
• He later said he submitted those messages to the FBI so any financial or geopolitical motive behind Kirk’s murder could be investigated

text:
A slowly warming world may be quietly nudging back the frozen boundaries of the North - the traditional margins of permafrost, arid tundra and the vast, mostly empty boreal forests.

However, studies now indicate that millions of square kilometres across Canada, Alaska, Scandinavia and Russia could cross critical thresholds for possible cultivation by the end of the century. 

Yet, transforming this vast northern frontier for farming or mining for minerals is not just a matter of waiting for the ice to melt—it would be a decades-long engineering and soil-transformation challenge.

The primary hurdle to a northern breadbasket is not temperature, but something called 'pedology' (the depleted chemistry of soils). Boreal and tundra soils are highly acidic, muddy and feature widespread peat bogs. They have very little deep root development, fungal growth or topsoil. 

Converting thawed land into tillable soil for grains like barley, rye, and oilseeds will need extensive soil conditioning and nutrient management. There would be no immediate crop harvests.

Ice-rich permafrost does not just melt into prairie with roaming buffalo, like the great plains of America. It would undergo 'thermokarst' degradation, collapsing into a mosaic of slumping ground, thermokarst lakes and wetland bogs. 

Heavy machinery cannot operate on such an unstable surface, meaning large-scale agriculture and master-planned settlements would have to concentrate in well-drained river valleys, ancient glacial outwash plains, and bedrock-stable corridors rather than open tundra.

The solar geometry of the far North has a unique biological dynamic. While 20-hour summer days offer unprecedented sunlight periods that drive plant growth cycles, the low angle of light means solar irradiance stays lower than traditional mid-latitude grain belts.

From an infrastructure perspective, opening the North would face severe logistical constraints. Thawing out muddy ground can shear road foundations, buckle rail lines and complicate building design. Realising the region's huge potential—such as access to critical minerals, rare earths and fresh water reserves—will need specific engineering techniques and heavy investment in road access.

Opening up the high latitudes echoes the great frontier eras of human history, but faces an engineering quagmire.

It could not happen overnight; but is more likely to be a series of centuries-long engineering challenges to liberate the far north. Human ingenuity, soil science, and structural engineering could only gradually reshape these wild, empty regions.

Passive cap-weight indexing is not a neutral market bet. It is an unhedged momentum trade.

​When mega-caps run, concentration feels effortless. When liquidity diffuses across the broader economy, cap-weight becomes a drag.

​Look at the S&P Dow Jones Indices data from our monthly tracking:

1.) ​The Breadth Breakout: More than 60% of S&P 500 stocks beat the index in both June (66.1%) and July (60.0%).

2.) ​The Performance Flip: S&P 500 Equal Weight finished July up 13.3% YTD vs. 10.1% for cap weight. A 3.2% spread in favor of the broad market.

3.) ​Tech Diffusion: Equal Weight Tech is outperforming cap-weighted Tech by 19% YTD. Capital expenditure is flowing beyond the platform giants into mid-tier suppliers and infrastructure.

​Why this matters for macro positioning:

​• In April and May, fewer than 27% of stocks could beat the index, and equal weight lagged by -4.5% and -2.6%.
• The moment index momentum stalled in June and July, broad breadth took over, generating +3.3% and +1.0% in relative equal-weight alpha.
• August has cooled toward 40% breadth month-to-date, showing this rotation is an active battleground, not a settled trend.

​Stock dispersion is trading near historic highs. When dispersion spikes, capital rotates and passive indexing concentrates your downside into yesterday's winners.

​Do not confuse passive market-cap concentration with true portfolio diversification. Focus on structural risk, evaluate capital flows objectively, and maintain disciplined rebalancing.

text:
The US military announced it had recovered a “flying disc” in 1947 - hours later, the Roswell story completely changed
In 1947, rancher William “Mack” Brazel discovered a strange debris field near Corona, New Mexico, containing rubber, foil, paper and sticks, along with what appeared to be evidence of a crash. After the discovery reached Roswell Army Airfield, the military publicly announced that it had recovered a “flying disc,” only for the explanation to quickly shift toward a weather balloon. Decades later, renewed interest in the incident transformed Roswell into one of history’s most famous UFO mysteries. A 1994 Air Force report offered another explanation: the wreckage was connected to Project Mogul, a top-secret program using enormous balloon arrays and sensitive equipment in an attempt to detect Soviet atomic tests from vast distances.

News24 N̶E̶E̶(Knee-Capped) Sky News’s Paul Murray, the Max Verstappen of hyperventilating horse shit, and that other mountebank Chris Kenny are both busy earning their Murdoch money spruiking the fantasy of a #PaulineHanson Tsunami.

All that while the other maladjusted, malcontent mountebanks from the #MSM are fiddling with each other's ferrets while tripping their balls off in some sort of acid-fuelled parallel universe.

Let me repeat: THE HANSON / ONE NATION RESULT IN SECRET HARBOUR IS NOT EXTRAORDINARY.

First, let's take a look at the loaded, reality-bending spin straight out of the Daily Telegraph stable today, where they desperately tried to frame a routine by-election result as some kind of unstoppable force: "Mr Albanese attempted to respond to the withering One Nation victory..."

A "withering" victory? That is textbook Murdoch myth-making, deliberately weaponised language designed to puff a localised ripple into a fake tidal wave. There is nothing withering, unprecedented, or extraordinary about it.

The very mainstream media machine (#MSM) that pumps a localised political ripple into a fantasy tsunami is operating its own mechanical wave machine to keep the fake tide rolling.

There is nothing new nor extraordinary in what we are currently seeing. Let’s look at the actual facts:

How predictable.
The very mainstream media machine (#MSM) that pumps a localised political ripple into a fantasy tsunami is now operating its own mechanical wave machine to keep the fake tide rolling.

There is nothing new nor extraordinary in what we are currently seeing. The recent primary vote result in Secret Harbour is being breathlessly peddled by commercial networks and News Corp stables as an unprecedented seismic shift. It isn't. It’s a historical rerun.

Let’s look at the actual facts:

🔹 The "Tsunami" That's Happened Before: Commentators are hyperventilating over a primary vote around 39% in a by-election. Yet back in the 1998 Queensland state election, One Nation didn't just win a single regional contest; they captured 11 seats in the state parliament and pulled a massive 22.68% state-wide primary vote. 

Furthermore, multiple One Nation candidates cleared primary vote percentages well into the 30s and high 40s in individual seats (such as Barambah, Burdekin, and Tablelands), and they finished second in 23 others, surpassing the Liberal Party's vote share and fundamentally scrambling the political landscape. #SecretHarbour is a ghost from the past, not a new frontier.

🔹 The Same Manufactured Spin:
One Nation supporters are screeching across social media that "winning Secret Harbour makes it legitimate to support One Nation." Bullshit. That is pure spin fed to them by the party marketing department to try and manufacture mainstream cover. Psychologically, what it actually reveals is that it, until a few days ago, it was too embarrassing to admit supporting them, so they are trying to normalise it.

🔹 Nothing New Under the Sun: Let’s not forget who we are dealing with. When Pauline Hanson first burst onto the federal scene as the candidate for Oxley, her total political experience was a single year on local council, and wait until you hear the background of that escapade in another article. 

Her playbook has never changed: target the vulnerable, attack #welfare systems, and exploit division. This isn't modern political genius; it's a recycled script. Back in 1872, prominent colonial figures like Henry Parkes were already using the exact same dog-whistling rhetoric, complaining about immigrant groups "disturbing this land of ours" and acting in separate organised masses. Hanson even has a history of taking direct aim at Irish communities with the same tired tropes. The target changes slightly over the decades, but the baseline bigotry remains identical.

🔹 The Run from Oxley & The Resulting Loss: Let's remember her track record when the heat actually turned up. After being elected to Oxley, electoral redistribution shifted the boundaries and turned her home turf into an unfavourable prospect. Rather than face the music, she abandoned Oxley, ran for the newly created rural seat of Blair at the 1998 federal election hoping for safer waters, and lost. She crashed out.

🔹 The Extremist Playbook & Vetting Failures: How is One Nation's candidate vetting going? Just like in 1998, when the party eagerly accepted the "support" of Adelaide-based neo-Nazi outfit National Action, whose leader offered up "bully boys" to defend meetings, nothing has cleaned up. The upcoming Victorian election, lest we forget: preselecting a candidate in 1998 with direct ties to a white supremacist and extremist group, the then Victorian NA chairperson Andrew Guild who was running for Deakin, and following public scrutiny and controversy regarding his links to the group and the party's association with extremist elements, Guild resigned from his candidacy. 

Nothing new

2026: News reports revealed that Tyler Green, the One Nation candidate for the South Australian seat of Mawson, had published more than a dozen extremist posts on social media

2019: Dean Smith, who ran for the federal seat of O’Connor as a candidate for Pauline Hanson’s One Nation in 2019 linked to “The Base” - Mr Smith, who didn’t proceed with his application to join The Base, can be heard in the calls praising National Socialist (Nazi) ideology and pledging to do anything to “save the race”.

2026: Man claiming to be One Nation branch official defended Hitler Youth and called Aboriginal people ‘stone age’ in racist posts

Nothing new!

🔹 The Inevitable Dumpster Fire: What the breathless daily bulletins always omit is the structural countdown that follows the hype. Within 12 months of that 1998 peak, One Nation turned into a complete internal dumpster fire. Infighting, policy contradictions, bitter disputes, and MPs defecting reduced the parliamentary line-up to a shell of itself. We are already watching those exact same internal fractures play out in real time.

What is happening right now is not an organic, unprecedented popularity surge. It is a media-fuelled feedback loop pumped by billionaires like Gina Rinehart and Rupert Murdoch, who has a very clear, vested commercial interest in crushing the Labor government.

None of this is new. The machine wants a drama to sell, and the far-right wants a vehicle to ride. History proves how it ends. The media machine just hopes you have a short memory.

Much of the #MSM has been reduced to a jumble sale full of chipped, stained teacups and one-armed teddy bears with clumped fur, where fur is still present, likely soaked in some babies’ once-soggy spittle, and now crusty jam. Potentially some puke. 

Those with short memories, considering voting One Nation and the ‘too dumb’ to know any better, are now owners of a rather stinky teddy bear named Ragged Rage, no relation to Rupert the bear. Oh, and a chipped teacup, made in China.

text: The thing is, Notre Dame doesn’t need this nonsense. I was fortunate to visit before the fire (in 2016) and my most profound thought was exactly that: what would a medieval peasant think when they walked in here? The light from the stained glass alone makes the space feel other worldly, a space designed to capture and move that light. Imagine a world where the only light you’ve ever seen is the sun, the moon, and flame but you enter a church to see light in every color of the rainbow! It’s we who are impoverished never getting to experience that, even worse thinking that splaying and LED light show on it offers a sense of transcendence.

text:
WHITE HEROIN: THE POISON BEHIND THE FORFEITURE

Letters from Stockholm — by Kio Amachree

There is a reason the United States government does not treat heroin trafficking as a paperwork offence. Heroin is not contraband. It is a death sentence sold by the gram.

Consider what this drug has done to America alone. Drug overdoses have killed over 1.25 million people in the United States since 1999, and over 105,000 Americans died from drug-involved overdose in 2023 alone. Heroin sits at the black heart of that catastrophe. Heroin-involved overdose deaths rose from 3,036 in 2010 to a peak of 15,469 in 2016 — a more than fivefold increase in six years. Even the recent decline in heroin deaths is no mercy: heroin deaths dropped largely because fentanyl displaced heroin in the supply, and fentanyl is far more potent and unpredictable. The heroin pipelines built in the 1980s and 1990s laid the rails on which fentanyl now travels.

Now consider Chicago, and the years that matter. According to US court documents, a white heroin trafficking network operated in Chicago and parts of Indiana, led by Adegboyega Mueez Akande, between 1988 and 1993. The network was actively trafficking white heroin into Illinois, and US court documents and affidavits from the IRS and FBI detailed how funds in bank accounts controlled by Bola Tinubu were tied to narcotics proceeds. The 1993 Illinois court judgment saw Tinubu forfeit 460,000 dollars from two bank accounts, after an investigation linked over 2 million dollars across several of his accounts to proceeds from the heroin trafficking of Akande and Abiodun Agbele. According to the affidavit, Akande controlled the operation of white heroin from Nigeria in conjunction with other individuals, and one individual identified as working with Akande was Bola Tinubu — and the Chicago address Tinubu gave on his account application was the same address used as the drop-off point for packages from Nigeria containing the white heroin. He was never criminally charged. But no innocent explanation has ever been offered for why the American government kept his money.

What was flooding into Chicago in those exact years? Between the 1980s and 1990s, the purity of heroin brought into the United States increased significantly, and Chicago stood among the largest, most lucrative white powder heroin markets in America. US intelligence was explicit about who moved it: Nigerian criminal groups transported Southeast and Southwest Asian heroin to Chicago by couriers aboard commercial aircraft, buses, and trains, and via package delivery services. The bodies followed. There were 803 drug-related deaths in Chicago in 1998, a 32 percent increase over 1995, and in 2000 heroin was a factor in more deaths in the Chicago area than any other illicit drug — 499 heroin-related deaths across the six-county metropolitan area in that single year.

And who died? Not the traffickers. Fierce competition pushed drug sales outdoors into areas with few legal jobs, including public housing complexes and distressed neighbourhoods on Chicago's West Side. Heroin became increasingly plentiful in low-income Black communities through what health experts call predatory marketing — and Black men born between 1951 and 1970 have always had the greatest risk of dying of overdoses, in their 20s, 30s and 40s, in Chicago, Baltimore, Washington and beyond. That is precisely the generation that was young and vulnerable when the Akande network operated. Decades later the wound has not closed: opioid-related death rates in Chicago remain highest for African Americans, and the majority of victims are on Chicago's West Side — Austin, East Garfield Park and West Garfield Park.

This is why the Greenspan v. FBI and DEA litigation before Judge Beryl Howell matters. This is why the release of the full investigative files matters. Nigeria is not being asked to relitigate 1993. Nigeria is being asked to look at what white heroin did to Black families in Chicago — grandmothers burying sons, children raised by aunts, a generation of men marked for early graves — and then to ask its President one simple question: what exactly was your money doing in that network's orbit?

A nation cannot preach drug enforcement at home while its highest office hides from a drug file abroad. Release the files. Let the record speak.

text:
Larak Strike and a Reply on Two Jordan Bases… Rival Accounts, Unsettled Results

Overnight Sunday-Monday the United States hit an IRGC navy site on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, the first on Iranian soil in about a month. The Guards then said a missile-and-drone operation targeted King Hussein and Azraq air bases in Jordan. Jordan said it intercepted eight missiles that entered its airspace. Three accounts—US, Iranian, Jordanian—meet, with no immediate independent damage check.

What happened on Larak

Iranian media reported blasts near the island. Tasnim cited early word of a drone attack, two killed and others wounded. An IRGC statement said fighters and civilians were killed and injured, called the attacker the “American-Zionist enemy,” and vowed to “punish the aggressor.” Spokesman Hossein Mohebbi wrote that a reply was coming.

Washington offered another version. An official told AP, anonymously, that forces hit launchers after seeing preparations to sow naval mines in the strait. Axios said two launch pads on Larak were struck. CENTCOM said in Arabic it took “limited, precise measures” against mine-laying units posing an “imminent threat,” and rejected the Guards’ label of aggression. US forces had finished clearing shipping-lane mines last week.

Jordan in the line of reply

Hours later the IRGC said its aerospace force staged a “combined operation” with ballistic missiles and drones, hitting “technical infrastructure, maintenance sites and enemy fighter positions” at King Hussein and Azraq as “punishing the aggressor” for Larak. It claimed “heavy losses,” warned new fire would meet harsher replies, and said the strike would not weaken Iran’s hold on Hormuz. Tasnim aired launch footage.

Amman did not confirm hits on the bases. An armed-forces spokesman said air defenses intercepted eight missiles that entered national airspace and destroyed them before they threatened people or property. Al Arabiya’s Jordan correspondent spoke of two salvos in about half an hour. Fox News cited a US source saying Iran attacked American forces in Jordan; most missiles were intercepted, with “no clear impact so far.”

What is still unsettled

Washington released no casualty toll or damage photos in Jordan. The Guards offered no independent proof that maintenance halls or fighter pads were destroyed. Jordan confined its result to eight intercepts inside its airspace, with no mention of debris on facilities or injuries. The gap between “heavy losses” and “no clear impact” remains a hole no single statement fills.

Hormuz and oil in the background

The Larak strike is tied to the waterway. Shipping data showed commodity vessels in Hormuz down to five a day as attacks on ships persist. Oil rose more than two percent after the raid. Washington cites mine-laying; Tehran cites control of Hormuz. The result so far is higher insurance and transit costs, not a visible military decision.

An economic track beside the field

The same day Scott Bessent said Washington would roll out weekly secondary sanctions starting with banks. Field blows and financial pressure now run together. Jordan is again an interception arena, not a declared party—between an Iranian account naming “US bases” on its soil and an official line about defending the skies.

Three questions remain: losses on Larak; whether anything fell on King Hussein and Azraq; and whether the eight intercepts were the full wave. Until independent figures or verifiable images appear, last night is a chain of statements more than a complete picture of the battle.

text:
Nuclear energy isn't just about electricity—it's about water. Nuclear desalination is one of the most under-discussed solutions to global water scarcity. A single nuclear reactor can produce enough desalinated water to supply a city of 1 million people while simultaneously generating electricity. The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region is leading the way, with Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar exploring nuclear desalination as a dual-purpose solution for power and water security. India is actively integrating desalination with its nuclear program, designing coastal nuclear plants with desalination capacity built in. The UAE's Barakah plant already has desalination capacity integrated into its design, and Russia is deploying floating nuclear plants with integrated desalination for remote coastal regions.

Africa is a prime market—250 million Africans lack access to clean water, and nuclear desalination can change that. Climate change is accelerating water stress globally, and the UN projects that by 2030, 700 million people will face severe water scarcity. Nuclear desalination offers reliable, 24/7 water production, large-scale capacity of millions of cubic meters per day, no greenhouse gas emissions, and energy and water security in one solution. Countries with coastlines and water stress should be looking at nuclear desalination. The technology is proven, the economics are improving, and the need is urgent.

Prof. V. K. Tripathi: “RSS Ideology Is Not the Ideology of Humanity”

“An ideology founded on hatred and the curtailment of freedom cannot be a good ideology.”

Prof. V. K. Tripathi, retired Professor Emeritus of Physics at IIT Delhi and a longtime campaigner for communal harmony, offers a blunt moral critique of the RSS ideology. His intervention is not merely about one organisation—it raises a larger question:

What should an ideology serve—identity or humanity?

Tripathi argues that any ideology built upon hatred, prejudice or suppression of freedom cannot be reconciled with humanism.

That position is consistent with his decades-long public work against communal polarisation. He has advocated dialogue, education and grassroots resistance to prejudice, arguing that people should be seen as human beings rather than reduced to labels of caste, religion, gender or nationality. 

His broader philosophy is especially relevant in a deeply polarised society:

Before Hindu or Muslim,
before upper caste or Dalit,
before Indian or foreigner,
before man or woman—
there is a human being.

And democracy requires that human being to possess freedom, dignity and equality.

The real test of any political or social ideology should therefore not be how effectively it creates an “us versus them”, but whether it expands our capacity for empathy, liberty, fraternity and justice.

Tripathi's message ultimately asks us to reject organised prejudice and recover something more fundamental:

 Don't allow ideology to make you less human.

His decades of activism have centred on exactly this principle—using education and dialogue to challenge prejudice and communal hatred. 

Humanity before hatred.
Freedom before authoritarianism.
Fraternity before communal division.
Constitutional democracy before ideological supremacy.

text: Paul I had a quick look at the paper itself: not the puff piece that is the press article. Andrew, Alyssa C., Chad W. Higgins, Mary A. Smallman, Maggie Graham, and Serkan Ates. 2021. “Herbage Yield, Lamb Growth and Foraging Behavior in Agrivoltaic Production System.” Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems 5 (April): 659175.  The senior author is Serkan Ates of Oregon State University who did his PhD at Lincoln.  The design looks okay with sufficient replication within and across years with a lot of detailed measurements.  However, it is essentially a put and take experiment that agronomists commonly use, and manages the herbage mass on offer at ~1300 kg DM/ha.  They did not test two or more stocking rates within each of  two systems examined, so theoretically they cannot estimate the optimal stocking rate and production per hectare for these two systems.  This latter experimental approach goes back a very long way and refer you to Jones, R. J., and R. L. Sandland. 1974. “The Relation between Animal Gain and Stocking Rate: Derivation of the Relation from the Results of Grazing Trials.” The Journal of Agricultural Science 83 (2): 335–42. While I think the paper is both interesting and useful, it cannot be expected to answer the questions you are asking.

rapture(n.)

c. 1600, "act of carrying off" as prey or plunder, from rapt + -ure, or else from French rapture, from Medieval Latin raptura "seizure, rape, kidnapping," from Latin raptus "a carrying off, abduction, snatching away; rape" (see rapt). The earliest attested use in English is with women as objects and in 17c. it sometimes meant rape (v.), which word is a close relation to this one.The sense of "spiritual ecstasy, state of mental transport or exaltation" is recorded by c. 1600 (raptures). The connecting notion is a sudden or violent taking and carrying away. The meaning "expression of exalted or passionate feeling" in words or music is from 1610s. The Rapture as an understanding of the Book of Revelation where faithful Christians will be lifted from the Earth to avoid the Apocalyptic Tribulation, is by 1852, after an interpretation by John Nelson Darby (1800 - 1882.)also from c. 1600
rapture(v.)

"to enrapture, put in a state of rapture," 1630s (implied in raptured), from rapture (n.). Related: Rapturing.also from 1630s

How and to whom did Jesus pay our ransom?
Answer
A ransom is something that is paid to provide for the release of someone who is held captive. Jesus paid our ransom to free us from sin, death, and hell. Throughout the books of Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy are found God’s requirements for sacrifices. In Old Testament times, God commanded the Israelites to make animal sacrifices for substitutionary atonement; that is, an animal’s death took the place of a person’s death, death being the penalty for sin (Romans 6:23). Exodus 29:36a states, "Each day you must sacrifice a young bull as an offering for the atonement of sin."

God demands holiness (1 Peter 1:15-16). God’s Law demands holiness. We cannot give God full holiness because of the sins we commit (Romans 3:23); therefore, God demands satisfaction of His Law. Sacrifices to Him satisfied the requirements. This is where Jesus comes in. Hebrews 9:12-15 tells us: "Once for all time he took blood into that Most Holy Place, but not the blood of goats and calves. He took his own blood, and with it he secured our salvation forever. Under the old system, the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a young cow could cleanse people’s bodies from ritual defilement. Just think how much more the blood of Christ will purify our hearts from deeds that lead to death so that we can worship the living God. For by the power of the eternal Spirit, Christ offered himself to God as a perfect sacrifice for our sins. That is why he is the one who mediates the new covenant between God and people, so that all who are invited can receive the eternal inheritance God has promised them. For Christ died to set them free from the penalty of the sins they had committed under that first covenant."

Also, read Romans 8:3-4, "The law of Moses could not save us, because of our sinful nature. But God put into effect a different plan to save us. Was Blondie's Debbie Harry really abducted by Ted Bundy?
Thomas Leatham
TUE 11TH OCT 2022 16.00 BST
There are several urban myths surrounding the lives of famous musicians. Take, for instance, the claims that Keith Richards snorted his father’s remains or that the first Kiss comic book is infused with the band members’ blood. There is also the claim that Debbie Harry of Blondie was once abducted by the notorious serial killer Ted Bundy.

Of the subject, Harry once explained: “I was trying to get a cab on the lower east side of the Village in New York, and it was kind of late. This was back in the early 1970s. I wasn’t even in a band then. I was trying to get across town to an after-hours club. A little white car pulls up, and the guy offers me a ride. So I just continued to try to flag a cab down. But he was very persistent, and he asked where I was going. It was only a couple of blocks away, and he said, ‘Well, I’ll give you a ride.'”

She added: “I got in the car, and it was summertime, and the windows were all rolled up except about an inch and a half at the top. So I was sitting there, and he wasn’t really talking to me. Automatically, I sort of reached to roll down the window and realized there was no door handle, no window crank, no nothing. The inside of the car was totally stripped out.”

Regardless of the mysterious person, it must have been a frightening experience for a young Harry. Getting into a car with a stranger who had no escape route immediately spells out trouble. Upon reflection, in later years, Harry felt adamant that the man was Bundy. She continued: “I got very nervous. I reached my arm out through the little crack and stretched down, and opened the car from the outside. As soon as he saw that, he tried to turn the corner really fast, and I spun out of the car and landed in the middle of the street.”

Detailing the incident further, Harry added: “It was right after his execution that I read about him. I hadn’t thought about that incident in years. The whole description of how he operated and what he looked like and the kind of car he drove and the time frame he was doing that in that area of the country fit exactly. I said, ‘My God, it was him.'”

However, many people have argued that Harry’s account does not match up with the other reports of Bundy’s whereabouts. Bundy was not known to have been in New York City in the early 1970s, nor was he said to have started abducting women until 1974. The fact that Harry says she wasn’t in a band at the time suggests that her story took place no later than 1973, a time in which she joined the Stilettos.

Bundy was also not known to have driven a “stripped out” vehicle without door handles and window levers. During the killing sprees in Salt Lake City and Seattle, Bundy was said to drive a normal-seeming Volkswagen Beetle. However, Harry still believes that the man who gave her the lift was Bundy. She said: “I’ve been debunked, actually, by those people that debunk you, or whatever. They say he wasn’t in New York at that time, but I think they’re really wrong because he had escaped and was travelling down the East Coast. I think that nobody has ever really investigated that. I didn’t know until later who it was. It was pretty scary.”

The Abomination Of Desolation
When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:) Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains: (Matthew 24:15-16)

Jesus is telling “ye” his disciples that they will see the abomination of desolation in the midst of answering the two questions from them. He would have said “whosoever” if he were speaking to a future generation.

He also expands the warning to “them which be in Judaea”, to those who were living at that time. They would see the abomination that he spoke of. He is not telling us that we will see it, but the author only includes us in the parenthetical close (whoso readeth, let him understand:) This is an explicit instruction for everyone to look in the book of Daniel to understand exactly what it was Jesus was telling those inhabitants of Judaea that they would see.

So we find the word abomination twice in the Book of Daniel:
(Dan 11:31) And arms shall stand on his part, and they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the daily sacrifice, and they shall place the abomination that maketh desolate.
(Dan 12:11) And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.
Daniel 11:31 is a reference to Antiochus Epiphanies among other acts, slaughtering a pig on the alter in the Temple, so here we get a definition:
An abomination that maketh desolate is a wrong sacrifice in the Temple.
In this instance it did not bring about the desolation of the Temple as it was not the Hebrew Nation which was directly responsible for the act nor was it made a “standing” practice.
Daniel 12:11 is the direct reference to what Jesus was was telling those in Judaea to be on the lookout for. When was this wrong sacrifice set up as a “standing” practice in the Temple? I will show you in the scripture:
Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God. But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people: The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing: (Hebrews 9:6-8)
This (underlined) was the authorized sacrifice for sin until the Messiah came and sacrificed Himself.
But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. John's witness is that Jesus said, “it is finished” before he gave up the ghost. Matthew records:
Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.
And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent; (Matthew 27:50-51)
What was finished? And what does the renting of the veil in the Temple represent? The sacrifice for sin, once for all was finished when Jesus gave up the ghost. The veil being rent in the temple signifies that Jesus was the way into the holiest of all so that the blood of goats and calves was no longer an acceptable sacrifice for sin. He caused the sacrifice and the oblation to cease in the middle of the week just as the Prophet Daniel foretold. He caused the sacrifice and the oblation to cease by the sacrifice of himself. Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in: behold, he shall come, saith the LORD of hosts. (Malachi 3:1)
Now if Jesus was the messenger of the covenant as foretold in Malachi, who better to confirm the covenant than the one who was to fulfill it, even the messenger of the covenant? When Paul was brought to trial before the Pharisees and the Sadducees he testified to the hope of the resurrection as a primary point of contention between the two religious sects. Historical Significance: It is most famously associated with Sargon of Akkad (24th century BCE), the legendary founder of the Akkadian Empire. Later, the Neo-Assyrian ruler Sargon II (8th century BCE) adopted the throne name to establish the legitimacy of his rule.
Sargis
Origin & Etymology: The name is the Classical Syriac and Armenian form of the Latin name Sergius. It originates from the ancient Roman gens (clan) Sergia, which etymologists suspect may connect to the Latin verb servare ("to guard" or "to preserve").
Sako

In the Middle East: Among Assyrians and Armenians, Sako is a popular, affectionate diminutive (or pet form) of the proper name Sargis.

$CRWD $NET  Yes, I think your skepticism is quite logically grounded. But let me refine it into a more precise formulation:

Cloudflare's Agentic AI narrative is real, but the financials have not yet proven that "Agentic AI is becoming a sufficiently large, sustainable new revenue engine for Cloudflare." Meanwhile, the market has already partially priced in that story.

This is structurally similar to what we were just discussing with CRWD.

**Let's start with the most important numbers:**

Cloudflare's latest Q2 2026:
- Revenue: $696.1M, +36% YoY
- Current RPO: +35%
- Full-year revenue guidance: ~+32%

So I would not say NET "has no growth" — 36% is actually solid growth.

But the issue is this:
That 36% growth in 2026 does not yet show any clear inflection point where "Agentic AI suddenly opens a second growth curve."  
The past several quarters have already been in the 30%-plus range.

So if investors are assigning NET a rich valuation today, the core thesis cannot simply be:
*"AI Agents are coming, therefore Cloudflare benefits."*

Because the financials have not yet told us that the full chain —
**Agent → Cloudflare revenue → accelerated growth**  
— has been validated.

**I particularly agree with your skepticism about whether Cloudflare can capture the biggest slice of the pie.**

Cloudflare's current narrative is actually very compelling:
- Agent
- ↓
- Accesses websites/APIs
- ↓
- Cloudflare AI Gateway
- ↓
- Authentication, permissions, monitoring, security, rate limiting
- ↓
- Cloudflare becomes the "toll highway" for Agents accessing the Internet.

It's a beautiful story.  
And Cloudflare has indeed been moving fast — AI Gateway, Agents, Workers, AI security, etc. The company's own data shows that AI-related crawler/agent traffic already accounts for a very meaningful portion of Internet traffic.

But —  
Your question is critical:

**Why would Google, Microsoft, or Amazon cede that "toll highway" to Cloudflare?**

I don't see a strong reason.

In fact, Cloudflare faces a rather daunting competitive landscape.

Assume more and more Agents in the future.  
An Agent accesses:
- Google Search / Gemini

Google can control the entire stack:
- Browser → Agent → Google Cloud → API → Website

Microsoft can control:
- Edge → Copilot → Azure → Entra → API Management

Amazon can control:
- AWS → Bedrock → API Gateway → IAM → Agent

Cloudflare, meanwhile, wants to be:
- Agent → Cloudflare → Internet

The question is: **Who owns the Agent?**  
Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.

**Who owns the cloud?**  
AWS, Azure, Google Cloud.

**Who owns enterprise identity?**  
Microsoft Entra, Google Workspace/IAM, etc.

**Who owns the browser?**  
Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge.

So what Cloudflare actually owns is **the edge layer of the Internet**.  
That has value, of course.  
But it is not a naturally defensible, irreplaceable position.

**Moreover, "AI Gateway" is not a particularly稀缺 (scarce) technology** — and I think this is where the market may be getting a bit overexcited.

At its core, an AI Gateway is simply:
> A control layer inserted between the Agent/AI application and the backend models/APIs.

There are already many competing approaches in the market:
- Cloudflare
- Microsoft Azure API Management
- AWS API Gateway / Bedrock
- Google Cloud
- Kong
- Various standalone AI Gateways

So what Cloudflare really needs to prove is:
**Why would enterprises ultimately funnel the bulk of their Agent traffic through Cloudflare, rather than directly through their existing cloud provider?**

That is far from settled at this point.

**So I would frame NET and CRWD together this way:**

You said:
*"Market enthusiasm is growing much faster than the fundamentals."*

I think that judgment holds — but to different degrees for each company.

**CRWD:**
- Revenue/ARR growth ~25%
- But the market is beginning to price it as an "AI Security super-winner"
- So valuation expansion has been very pronounced.

**NET:**
- Revenue growth 36%
- So its underlying fundamentals are actually stronger than CRWD's.
- But the market is now also assigning it an additional premium for:
  - Agentic Internet infrastructure

So you now have:
- Traditional Cloudflare business value
- PLUS AI/Agent future value
- PLUS AI Gateway future value
- PLUS Agentic Internet future value  
— all stacked into today's stock price.

**This creates a very dangerous problem:**

Suppose over the next three years:
- NET revenue: $2.9B → $3.8B → $4.9B

That looks great on paper.  
But if the market later realizes that:
> Agentic AI did *not* turn Cloudflare's growth from 30% into 50%,

then investors will say:
*"Wait — so Agents are just helping Cloudflare sustain ~30% growth, not creating a massive new TAM."*

At that point:
- The business doesn't crash,
- But the multiple compresses from very high → normal,
- And the stock can still fall significantly.

**This is indeed very similar in nature to CRWD.**

I would summarize the current market narratives for both as:

- **CRWD:** AI attacks are getting stronger → AI Security TAM explodes → CRWD becomes the primary winner.
- **NET:** AI Agents are proliferating → Agentic Internet explodes → Cloudflare becomes the on-ramp for Agent traffic.

Both stories share a common flaw:
> **"The trend is real" ≠ "This company will capture enough of the monetization."**

That is exactly the core point you've been pressing on.

**And I think NET has one potentially larger risk than CRWD:**

CRWD at least has a well-established, mature core market:
- Endpoint + Identity + Cloud Security

AI is simply adding incremental demand to that existing market.

Cloudflare's valuation, by contrast, is increasingly relying on:
> *"A structural change in how the Internet is accessed in the future."*

If that prediction holds, NET could be tremendous.  
But if Agent activity ultimately remains largely within:
- Google's / Microsoft's / AWS's / OpenAI's own ecosystems — rather than flowing through Cloudflare —

then Cloudflare could find that:
> Agent traffic grew 10x, but its own revenue only grew modestly.

This is the classic case of:
> **Traffic growth ≠ Monetization growth.**

And this, in my view, is the single most important caution for investing in NET.

**That said, I will offer one defense of Cloudflare:**

It is not purely a "story stock."  
The Q2 numbers — 36% revenue growth, 35% Current RPO growth — are real, and the company continues to expand its large-customer base.

So I would not classify NET as:
> *"An AI concept stock with no fundamentals."*

Rather, I would categorize it as:
> *"A very solid growth company with strong fundamentals — plus the market is already pricing in a large AI option value ahead of time."*

The real question is: **how much is that AI option actually worth?**

**So if I string together your entire logic, I actually arrive at a very interesting ranking:**

- **Anthropic**  
  → AI *is* the product  
  → Revenue growing extremely fast  
  → $2T valuation is expensive, but has some fundamental explanatory room

- **NET**  
  → AI is a significant potential incremental driver  
  → Current growth 36%  
  → Agent monetization not yet proven  
  → High valuation carries a clear AI option premium

- **CRWD**  
  → AI is a demand catalyst for security  
  → ARR only ~25%  
  → Agentic Security has not proven CRWD has exclusivity  
  → Valuation premium is more dependent on market sentiment

So from the angle you're exploring —
> *"Which AI stocks show the widest gap between fundamentals and market enthusiasm?"*

— I would currently put **CRWD ahead of NET** on that list.

But if NET's valuation continues to expand with the "Agentic Internet" narrative, while revenue growth over the next few quarters remains only ~30%, I will grow increasingly cautious that NET could experience a similar dynamic to CRWD:

> **"Story gets grander → Numbers don't accelerate in sync → Multiple eventually compresses."**

And this is also why I think your earlier observation about a potential **Anthropic IPO** is very worth watching —  
it may force portfolio managers to ask, for the first time, a very direct question:

> *"Am I buying actual AI, or am I buying a story about AI making this company bigger?"*

Once that distinction starts to enter institutional valuation models, the multiple expansion for second-order AI beneficiaries like CRWD and NET could very well reverse.

🌱 Soybean Mark Summary — 28 Aug 2026

📈 Soybean futures surged again: CME November soybeans rose 20¢/bu (+1.58%) to $12.88/bu.
🥣 Derived products led the rally: October soymeal gained 2.42% to $342.50/st, while soyoil jumped 3.80% to $70.82/lb.
🇺🇸 RIN policy speculation supported prices: Markets expect possible US government compensation for crushers/farmers following expanded small-refinery exemptions involving 1.8 billion RINs.
🚢 Strong US export demand: USDA reported fresh flash sales of 180,000 tonnes to China and 226,000 tonnes to undisclosed destinations, alongside additional soymeal sales.
🇧🇷 Brazilian premiums weakened: Higher futures and a stronger Brazilian real pressured FOB Paranaguá premiums, with October paper down 12¢/bu to +150¢/bu over November futures.
🇨🇳 Dalian market mixed: January soyoil rose 1.55% to ¥8,920/t, while January soymeal fell 0.83% to ¥3,312/t.
🚢 China continued buying: Five soybean cargoes for November–April loading were purchased from Brazil and the US. Brazilian April cargo traded at +110¢/bu over May CME, while US November cargoes traded around +308–318¢/bu over November CME.
🏦 Sinograin kept selling stocks: Of 290,794 tonnes offered on Aug. 26, 222,782 tonnes were sold. Total imported soybean sales over the preceding five weeks reached 1.57 million tonnes.
📅 Another Sinograin auction: 68,000 tonnes are scheduled for sale on Sept. 2, potentially creating more storage space for incoming US beans.
🇺🇸🇨🇳 US-China buying expectations remain important: China has purchased roughly 10 million tonnes of US soybeans for Q4 2026 loading since early July, with markets watching the planned Sept. 24 Xi–Trump summit.
🏭 China crush remained high: Crushers processed about 2.22 million tonnes of soybeans in the week to Aug. 21.
⚠️ Brazilian crush margins deteriorated: September/October Brazilian soybean crush margins fell to -¥280 to -¥265/t, down ¥80–85/t week on week.
💰 US beans remained much more expensive into China: September US soybeans were assessed at around ¥4,853/t landed, duty paid, approximately ¥474/t above comparable Brazilian beans.
📊 CFR China Brazil premium: October soybean CFR China was assessed at 306¢/bu over November CME, down 3¢/bu, equivalent to approximately $580/t.
🔑 Key takeaway: Bullish futures momentum is being driven by strong soymeal/soyoil performance, renewed US export sales and expectations of increased China-US soybean trade, while weak Brazilian crush margins and softer origin premiums highlight pressure in the physical market.

What are the new heaven and the new earth?
Answer
In Revelation 21:1, John sees something spectacular: “Then I saw ‘a new heaven and a new earth,’ for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away.” This new earth and new heaven are sometimes referred to as the “eternal state.” As seen in Revelation chapters 21—22, the new earth will be the eternal dwelling place of believers in Jesus Christ. Scripture gives us a few details of the new heaven and new earth.

The current heaven and earth have long been subject to God’s curse because of mankind’s sin. All creation “has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth” (Romans 8:22) as it awaits the fulfillment of God’s plan and “the children of God to be revealed” (verse 19). Heaven and earth will pass away (Mark 13:31), and they will be replaced by the new heaven and the new earth. At that time, the Lord, seated on His throne, says, “I am making everything new!” (Revelation 21:5). In the new creation, sin will be totally eradicated, and “there shall be no more curse” (Revelation 22:3, NKJV).

The new heaven and new earth are also mentioned in Isaiah 65:17; 66:22; and 2 Peter 3:13. Peter says that the new heaven and new earth will be “where righteousness dwells.” Isaiah says that “the former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.” Things will be completely new, and the old order of things, with the accompanying sorrow and tragedy, will be gone.

The new earth will be free from sin, evil, sickness, suffering, and death. It will be earth as God originally intended it to be, prior to the curse of sin. It will be Eden restored.

A major feature of the new earth will be the New Jerusalem. John calls it “the Holy City . . . coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband” (Revelation 21:2). This glorious city, with its streets of gold and pearly gates, is situated on a new, glorious earth. The tree of life will be there (Revelation 22:2). This city represents the final state of redeemed mankind, forever in fellowship with God: “God’s dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God. . . . His servants will serve him. They will see his face” (Revelation 21:3; 22:3–4).

In the new heaven and new earth, Scripture says, there are seven things notable for their absence—seven things that are “no more”:
• no more sea (Revelation 21:1)
• no more death (Revelation 21:4)
• no more mourning (Revelation 21:4)
• no more weeping (Revelation 21:4)
• no more pain (Revelation 21:4)
• no more curse (Revelation 22:3)
• no more night (Revelation 22:5)

The creation of the new heaven and new earth brings the promise that God “will wipe every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 21:4). This event comes after the tribulation, after the Lord’s second coming, after the millennial kingdom, after the final rebellion, after the final judgment of Satan, and after the great white throne judgment. The brief description of the new heaven and new earth is the last glimpse into eternity that the Bible gives.

The story of Tom Brown, the retired engineer that became 'apple hunter', rescuing over 1,000 'lost' varieties in the last 25 years

Retired chemical engineer, he began his quest to find and preserve lost apple varieties around more than 25 years ago. 

The man who owns an apple orchard called Heritage Apples in Clemmons, North Carolina, USA has re-discovered over 1000 rare varieties of apples.

His Heritage Apples showcase at least 600 of them. He has been working so that the heirloom apples of Appalachia in the Eastern United States do not disappear with time.

Popularly known as the Apple-Hunter, Tom grows around 60 varieties of apples each year on his farm and sells around 1000 trees. To encourage more preservation, Brown offers to discounts on the purchase of rarer heritage varieties. Trees from Georgia, Virginia, North Carolina and a few other places have found their forever homes in his orchard.

text:
If you are still building your NIW petition using a generic template from 2024, you may be setting yourself up for an unnecessary RFE or worse.

The biggest mistake tech professionals make is thinking that USCIS is impressed by their job title, salary, or employer alone.

That is not how the NIW standard works.

Here are 3 things that matter:

1️⃣ Your job title is not your proposed endeavor.
“I’m a Senior Software Engineer at a major tech company” describes your employment.
It doesn't necessarily establish national importance.

Your petition should explain what you intend to accomplish and why that work matters beyond your current employer.

2️⃣ Your degree is not the NIW.

A Master's degree or Ph.D. may help establish the underlying EB-2 qualification.

But the NIW requires you to satisfy the three Dhanasar prongs.

Your evidence should demonstrate that you are well positioned to advance your proposed endeavor.

That can include research, publications, patents, technical leadership, measurable project outcomes, industry adoption, expert recommendations, and other relevant evidence.

3️⃣ NIW is more than a way to avoid PERM.

Yes, an approved NIW can eliminate the traditional job-offer and labor-certification requirement.
But PERM delays alone don't establish national interest.

The real question is:

Why should the United States waive those requirements for YOU and YOUR proposed endeavor?

A weak petition says:

“I’m highly educated, experienced, well paid, and work for a great company.”

A stronger petition explains:

“Here is the problem I intend to solve, why it matters to the United States, why I am positioned to solve it, and why waiving the normal requirements benefits the national interest.”

That's the difference between submitting a résumé and building an NIW strategy.

If you're an engineer, AI professional, cybersecurity specialist, researcher, semiconductor expert, or tech founder considering an EB-2 NIW, start with your proposed endeavor not a template.

Start with the endeavor.

Then build the evidence around it.

text:
🚨 $INPST (InPost) Q2 2026 Earnings  
Beat the quarter…  
but the real story is the guidance cut + takeover overlay 👀  
📊 KEY METRICS (Q2 2026)  
🔹 Revenue: PLN 4.178bn (+18% YoY) vs ~PLN 4.100bn cons 🟢  
🔹 Adj. EBITDA: PLN 1.043bn (+4.3% YoY) vs ~PLN 1.01–1.019bn cons 🟢  
🔹 Adj. EBITDA margin: 25.0% (vs 24.8% cons) — still −3.3pp YoY 🟡  
🔹 EBIT: PLN 313m (−43% YoY) — slight miss 🔻  
🔹 Net profit: PLN 93m (−30% YoY) — miss vs ~PLN 121m cons 🔻  
🔹 H1 revenue: PLN 8.04bn (+24% YoY)  
🔹 H1 adj. EBITDA: PLN 1.945bn (~flat YoY, +0.3%)  

👉 Core takeaway:  
Top line and core EBITDA beat. Profitability below the line and full-year earnings power got weaker.

📈 GROWTH ENGINE (CORE STORY)  
🟢 Parcel-locker / out-of-home network still scaling across Europe  
🟢 International mix rising (Poland cash cow + Eurozone + UK/Ireland)  
🟢 Volume/revenue still mid-teens+ even after a heavy investment year  
🟢 ~19k new APMs still planned (3k Poland / 11k Eurozone / 5k UK & Ireland)  

👉 This is:  
pan-European last-mile / locker infrastructure play, not a mature post office.

🚀 STRATEGIC OVERLAY (MAJOR SHIFT)  
🟢 Target of recommended all-cash offer: FedEx + Advent (+ A&R, PPF)  
🟢 Offer: €15.60/share → €7.8bn equity / $9.2bn deal value  
🟢 Capex trimmed to ~PLN 2.1bn from 2.4bn — still growth spend, just less aggressive  
🟢 Network plan trimmed only slightly (19k APMs vs prior 20k)  

👉 Impact:  
public-market story is now dual-track: operating results vs deal close / regulatory path.

⚡ WHAT’S HAPPENING?  
• Q2: growth still there, adj. EBITDA slightly ahead of Street  
• Mix/investment/UK transformation still crushing reported EBIT and net income  
• Management no longer thinks it can hold adj. EBITDA flat for FY26  
• Capex and locker rollout modestly de-risked, leverage still drifts up  

👉 This is:  
growth-at-the-expense-of-margins year, with a bid putting a ceiling/floor under the stock.  

📉 PROFITABILITY (THE WEAK POINT)  
🔻 FY adj. EBITDA guidance: flat → mid-single-digit % decline  
🔻 Q2 EBIT −43% YoY; net profit −30% YoY and a clear miss  
🔻 Group margin mid-20s vs much fatter historic Poland margins  
🔻 UK/Yodel integration + pricing/volume investments still eating earnings  
🔻 H1 adj. EBITDA basically unchanged vs last year despite +24% H1 sales  

👉 Translation:  
core EBITDA “beat” is real. Quality of earnings and FY trajectory are not.  

📅 2026 GUIDANCE (THE CUT)  
🔹 Adj. EBITDA: mid-single-digit decline (was flat) 🔻  
🔹 Capex: PLN 2.1bn (was 2.4bn) 🟢 for cash, 🔻 for growth pace  
🔹 APM additions: 19,000 (was 20,000)  
🔹 Net leverage: a bit higher than YE 2025  

👉 Important:  
they are still investing — just admitting the P&L cannot absorb the original plan.  

🧠 WHAT’S ACTUALLY WORKING  
🟢 Revenue still compounding at high-teens in Q2 / mid-20s in H1  
🟢 Slight beat on the metric the market actually watches (adj. EBITDA)  
🟢 Poland remains the high-margin engine funding expansion  
🟢 Eurozone locker rollout still the long-term share-gain story  
🟢 Bid from FedEx/Advent validates the network strategically  

⚠️ WEAK SPOTS  
🔻 Guidance cut on the key profit metric  
🔻 Reported EBIT / net income collapsing on D&A, mix, UK costs  
🔻 Margin compression is structural this year, not a one-quarter blip  
🔻 FCF still pressured even after the capex trim  
🔻 Deal risk: timing, approvals, what happens if the offer fails  
🔻 Execution risk in UK transformation and Eurozone density build  

👉 Still:  
not a clean “beat and raise” print. It’s a “beat and cut.”  

🧠 MARKET SIGNAL  
👉 This is a European e-commerce logistics compounder  
• Scale story intact  
• Earnings power being sacrificed for network  
• Equity value currently anchored more by the €15.60 bid than by FY26 EBITDA  

🔥 BULL vs BEAR  
🟢 Bull Case  
• International volumes keep compounding  
• Capex cut protects cash without killing the network plan  
• FedEx partnership / bid crystallizes strategic value  
• Poland cash generation funds the rest of Europe  

🔴 Bear Case  
• Mid-single-digit EBITDA decline is the start, not the trough  
• UK stays a drag longer than modeled  
• Leverage ticks up into a higher-rate / deal-limbo period  
• If the takeover slips, the stock has to re-rate on weaker FY26 profits  

💭 CONCLUSION  
$INPST still grew, still beat adj. EBITDA…  
👉 but management just told you 2026 profits go down, not sideways.  

The quarter is fine.  
The guide is the story.  
The FedEx/Advent offer is the price anchor.  

👀 KEY QUESTION  
Can InPost keep taking share in lockers while EBITDA falls — and does the consortium still want the asset at €15.60 if the earnings base is shrinking?

text:
The Indian opposition is going to have a fun time for a while in the wake of the Delhi demonstrations.  

They will offer themselves as the alternative to the BJP, promising lots of good white collar jobs which Modi has failed to provide.

Maybe they will get power at the centre and in the states.

Then they will find themselves stuck.    How to deliver the promised jobs?   

India's Nehruite economy is extremely hard to change fundamentally.   

Indian factories cannot expand fast because bigger factories cannot lay off workers or hire them easily due to tough labour rules imposed by Nehru.   Unions will defend those rules ruthlessly.  Rahul Gandhi can do nothing about that.  His party opposes a more flexible labour code.

Indian workers are perpetually on strike, deterring domestic and foreign investment.  Rahul Gandhi cannot change that.

Land for factories and infrastructure is hard to buy in India because too much compensation is demanded and there are endless court battles.  Rahul Gandhi cannot change that.   In fact his party helped stop BJP led attempts to make land purchases for industry easier.

High protectionism imposed by Nehru means Indian firms lack the incentive to produce goods of quality good enough to sell in the world market.  So India is poor at exporting goods.  The system benefits Indian industrialists who fund political parties.  Rahul Gandhi cannot change that.

More good jobs in education and health care needs a lot more government spending on both areas.  But India cannot tax rich farmers and so governments do not have the money for such spending.  Nehru perpetuated the no tax of rich farmers policy.  No government dares to abolish it.  Rahul Gandhi can do nothing about it.

So what can Rahul Gandhi offer?

Caste quotas in jobs and education.  This is the opposite of what the upper caste students who are protesting want.

Heigh ho!   

Modi has no answers.    He is on a sticky wicket.

But so is Rahul Gandhi and the opposition.

If they win there will be short term euphoria and then complete disillusionment. 

The cocky Cockroach Party is doomed to disappointment.

No government and no party has easy answers for India.

How strange that no-one in the Indian and foreign press is pointing out these obvious facts!

ASTANA, KAZAKHSTAN - Kazakhstan is moving forward with plans to acquire Russia’s Su-57 stealth fighters, a purchase that would introduce fifth generation combat aircraft into its fleet for the first time. The deal, discussed for several years and reinforced by recent defence reports, is expected to replace ageing Su-27s and eventually MiG-31 interceptors as the country modernises its air force.

Kazakhstan’s current inventory is built around Soviet and Russian aircraft, including Su-30SM fighters and upgraded MiG-31BM interceptors. Integrating the Su-57 will require new maintenance facilities, secure data systems and specialised pilot training, marking one of the largest aviation upgrades in the country’s history.

If deliveries proceed as planned, Kazakhstan would become the second former Soviet republic after Russia to operate a fifth generation fighter and one of only a few countries worldwide with access to such technology. The move also deepens defence cooperation with Moscow at a time when China’s J-35 and other regional platforms are expanding their presence in Central Asia.

The Su-57 offers long range and compatibility with advanced missile systems, though it is generally considered less sophisticated than the US F-35 or China’s J-35. Kazakhstan’s decision reflects both its longstanding defence ties with Russia and its effort to maintain a modern air combat capability in a region where neighbours are rapidly upgrading their fleets.

The first aircraft are expected to arrive within the next two years, placing Kazakhstan among the earliest foreign operators of Russia’s newest fighter.

text:
11 days. One striking coincidence. But coincidence is not evidence of a deal.

On 18 August 2026, Uzbekistan's Technological Metals Complex (TMK) confirmed that it had met representatives of the Adani Group to discuss potential investment in mining and mineral-processing projects, including geological exploration and possible future industrial development. 

On 29 August, Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Uzbekistan for a state visit. The Indian government says the visit was intended to deepen the India–Uzbekistan strategic partnership, including trade, investment, defence, digital connectivity, energy and education. 

That timing is certainly worth asking questions about.

But we should not turn timing into proof of a quid pro quo.

There is, however, another independently verifiable fact that deserves attention.

India signed a long-term agreement with Uzbekistan in 2019 for 1,100 MTU of natural uranium ore concentrates for 2022–2026. 

And in a Lok Sabha reply dated 26 March 2025, the Department of Atomic Energy stated that 600 MTU had been supplied out of the contracted 1,100 MTU. The same reply recorded imports of 350 MTU in 2023–24 and 250 MTU in 2024–25 from Navoiyuran. 

So the transcript's basic arithmetic is right:

600 ÷ 1,100 ≈ 54.5%.

But there is an important qualification: the official figure of 600 MTU was reported as of March 2025, while the contract runs through 2026. It therefore does not prove that Uzbekistan ultimately failed to deliver the remaining 500 MTU by the end of the contractual period.

And this uranium agreement predates the August 2026 Adani meeting by seven years.

That matters.

The real democratic question

India's nuclear programme has a substantial future uranium requirement. The same parliamentary answer estimated about 9,000 MTU of imported natural uranium demand for safeguarded PHWRs during 2025–2033. 

So India's relationship with uranium-producing countries is strategically important.

But strategic importance makes transparency more important—not less.

If private Indian companies are simultaneously exploring mineral investments in Uzbekistan while the Indian government is negotiating energy and resource cooperation with Uzbekistan, citizens are entitled to ask:

What exactly is being negotiated?
Which companies are involved?
Which minerals are covered?
Are any uranium interests involved?
Were any government officials involved in facilitating private investment?
Were any concessions, contracts or guarantees offered?
And are the terms being disclosed appropriately?

Those questions are legitimate.

What is not legitimate is declaring that “Adani met Uzbekistan on August 18, therefore Modi went there on August 29 to secure Adani's uranium deal” without documentary evidence.

We don't need conspiracy theories. We need documents.

Adani's Uzbekistan meeting is real.
Modi's Uzbekistan visit is real.
India's 1,100-MTU uranium agreement with Uzbekistan is real.
The government acknowledged that only 600 MTU had been supplied by March 2025.

What has not been established is a causal link between these events.

So let's demand the evidence—not manufacture the conclusion.

In a democracy, public resources, strategic minerals and foreign-policy decisions must withstand scrutiny.

Ask for the contracts.
Ask for the beneficiaries.
Ask for the terms.
Ask who negotiated what.
Follow the money.
Follow the documents.

Because accountability is strongest when our criticism is as rigorous as the evidence we demand from those in power.

text:
Lesson 9 from the Divine Office for the Feast of Saints Felix and Adauctus, Martyrs.
.
Felix was arrested in the reign of the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, on the charge of having embraced the Christian Faith, and was brought to the temple of Serapis. When he was ordered to offer sacrifice, he spat in the face of the brazen idol, which thereupon fell down. When this happened a second and third time in the temples of Mercury and Diana, he was accused of impiety and magic, and tortured upon the rack. It was not long, however, before he was led out to the second mile-stone upon the road to Ostia, to be smitten with the axe. As they were on their way thither, they chanced to meet a certain Christian, who, when he knew that Felix was going to finish his testimony, said aloud: I live by the same law as he doth; I worship the same Christ Jesus. And therewith he kissed Felix, and they were beheaded together, upon the 30th day of August. What the name of the second person was the Christians never knew, and he is therefore honoured under the title of Adauctus, that is, Himself-who-was-added; as he was added to the company of the Holy Martyr Felix in winning of the crown.

Calling the Church His Body does not settle which altar, which baptism, and which officers He actually claimed.

Continuity is the thing that must be shown, not assumed.

They are how a Prophet still speaks, a Priest still mediates, and a King still organizes His house.

This was @grok's take when I asked:

Yes — this is the issue Baker’s post largely skipped, and it is the one that still generates the most visceral neighbor complaints.

The noise is real. It is not usually “factory loud” in the OSHA-hearing-damage sense. It is a constant 24/7 mechanical signature that many people find uniquely hard to live with: rooftop and yard cooling fans, chillers, cooling towers, transformers, and (at some sites) on-site gas turbines. Periodic generator load tests are much louder and can carry a long way at night.

What people actually describe is a vacuum-like whine, a distant-highway roar that never stops, or a low tonal hum / pressure sensation that standard A-weighted meters under-report. That last point matters: a facility can meet a 50–55 dBA ordinance and still be miserable because low-frequency and tonal content travels farther and is more annoying than broadband traffic noise at the same number.

How bad it is depends almost entirely on design and siting:

Poor cases (crypto-to-AI conversions, tight setbacks, unenclosed rooftop arrays, off-grid turbine campuses) have produced lawsuits in Michigan, Wisconsin (Microsoft Fairwater), New Jersey, Mississippi (xAI turbines), and elsewhere. Residents report sleep disruption; some operators have been fined or offered to buy homes.
Virginia’s 2024 JLARC review — the most systematic independent look — found that even facilities that drew complaints typically measured 40–59 dB at nearby homes. Many data centers generate no noise complaints at all. That is well below conversation level and far below hearing-damage thresholds, but it is still a constant presence.
Well-structured new projects are now commonly designed to ~45–55 dBA at the property line, with larger setbacks, enclosed equipment, acoustic louvers, perimeter walls/berms, and scheduled daytime-only generator tests. Some operators have retrofitted existing sites (fan shrouds, sound walls, chiller attenuation) after complaints.

So the honest version of Baker’s thesis applied here: noise is the lagging concern. Water, tax structure, and job mix have clearer “solved if structured right” answers. Sound is solvable with the same discipline — distance, enclosure, frequency-specific barriers, and enforceable nighttime limits that include low-frequency/tonal criteria, not just dBA — but it is not yet standard everywhere, and older or cheaply built sites are still producing genuine quality-of-life problems.

If a town is approving a campus, the useful asks are: modeled levels at the nearest bedroom window (not just the fence), independent post-commissioning measurement, enclosed cooling and generators as a permit condition, and a retrofit obligation if those numbers are missed. That is how this one gets into the same “addressed” bucket as the issues Baker listed.

A RUMOR MOVED WORKDAY $WDAY THREE TIMES MORE THAN ITS OWN EARNINGS DID:

Workday WDAY at $204.72, +$11.15 / +5.76% from Thursday's $193.57 close. Friday's regular close; US markets reopen Monday 9:30am ET.

It reported a better quarter than expected, the stock rose, and it still ended the week below where a two-week-old rumor had already put it.

Picture a lemonade stand. Two things change what it is worth: selling more cups, or a rich neighbor offering to buy the whole stand. The second moves the number more, and the second can be taken back.

First, the cups. Workday, of Pleasanton, California, sells the software big companies use to run payroll, hiring and staff records. It reported Thursday after the close, for the quarter ended July 31. Revenue - the money coming in the door - was $2.65B vs $2.64B expected, +12.8% from a year earlier; adjusted profit $2.75 a share vs $2.61 expected. Subscription revenue, the part arriving on repeating contracts, was $2.47B, +13.9%.

Now the neighbor. On August 13, Reuters reported that Silver Lake, a private investment firm with no shares of its own to trade, was in talks to buy Workday outright. The stock closed that day at $206.45, +$31.16 / +17.78%, its best day in ten years, on news Workday never published. Friday's close is still $1.73 under it. There is still no agreement, no price and no date; Workday says it does not comment on speculation.

One fact sits under both halves: Workday bills customers by how many employees they have, so the worry has been that AI means fewer staff and less money. Friday pushed back. AI products drove more than a quarter of newly signed contract value, across 5,500-plus customers.

WHERE THESE SIT

Workday is on none of the six Len5es. Quality-Value wants a strong business at a fair price, and strong is not the problem - roughly 42 times the last year of profit is. A real markdown with the growth intact would change that.

Paycom Software at $238.53, +$1.49 / +0.63% from Thursday's $237.04, is fifth on the Momentum Len5, which watches names already climbing on their own news. The Oklahoma City payroll software maker touched a 52-week high of $242.50 on Friday, and its August 5 quarter is why: revenue $531.2M, +9.8%, profit $2.34 a share against $1.58 a year earlier. It bills by employee too. Slipping back into the middle of its summer range would break the fit.

Whether the neighbor ever makes a real offer is the thing to keep an eye on. The earnings half already happened. The $1.73 gap is a maybe.
